# Propose: the slice list, the proposal and its refusals

Read for [`fgos-cook`](../SKILL.md). `fgos workflow propose` is read-only: it writes
no case event, opens no case and runs nothing, so a refused or unapproved proposal
costs no dispatch. You supply judgment (the slices); it supplies arithmetic and
lookup (kinds, frame, checks, question, commands). Run it with stdin closed.

## The slice list

A JSON file passed with `--slices`, with `--plan <path>` naming the plan and
`--guide <id>` (default `coding/feature`), `--worktree` and `--branch` to override the
case worktree (`../<slug>-worktree`, `case/<slug>`).

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `request` (top level, optional) | The case outcome in one paragraph; defaults to "Deliver the plan at <plan>". |
| `id` | Lowercase letters, digits and dashes; unique. |
| `objective` | What the slice does and the plan phase and decisions it rests on. It is the brief of the run. |
| `writes` | Repository paths the slice may change, no commas. A directory or glob is expanded to real files; empty means a read-only slice. |
| `verify` | One narrow pass/fail command; required for a writing slice. |
| `dependsOn` | Ids of slices that must come first (real dependencies only; the plan's order is a hint). |
| `raise` | `{ "rigor": "...", "reason": "..." }`: raises a writing slice above its table rigor. Never lowers it. |
| `followUp` | `{ "capability": "...", "pattern": "..." }`: a review after the slice. A docs slice already carries one. |
| `earlyReview` | `true` adds an early read-only review of the slice before the rest is built on it. |
| `inputs` | Repository files given to the slice as `--input` (locked decisions, phase files); must exist. |
| `capability`, `pattern`, `rigor`, `activity` | Read-only slices only. A writing slice takes capability, pattern and rigor from the table. |

A slice's kind, capability, pattern and rigor come from its write paths
(`domains/coding/slice-kinds.yaml`): the highest rigor among its paths wins. A
contract, locked law, Rust crate, lock file, identity or write door is never below
`high`. `propose` also adds, visibly, the test files that exercise the code a slice
changes (`expansions`); do not add them by hand.

## A request with no plan

`fgos workflow propose --request "<text>" --writes <paths> --verify "<cmd>"` sizes it
and answers with a `kind`: `single-run` (one small writing task: the proposal is a
worktree plus one `fgos run`, no case), `manifest-needed` (bigger or riskier: write the
slice list), or `shape-plan-first` (no path named: shape the plan first). It does not
combine with `--slices`, `--plan` or `--guide`.

## The proposal

Text output prints the owner's question first (five parts, in Vietnamese) and then the
commands. With `--json` the same proposal is under `data`: `ok`, `frame`, `breakdown`,
`slices`, `ownerFirst`, `parked`, `expansions`, `refusals`, `questions`, `commands`.
Exit code 0 when `ok`; 1 when the proposal itself carries refusals (read
`data.refusals`); 4 for a call that is wrong before any proposal exists
(`propose-source`, `propose-slices-unreadable`, `propose-guide-missing`): a message on
stderr and no proposal. A refusal leaves `frame` null and `commands` empty: nothing is
offered for approval until every refusal is fixed.

After the owner approves, run `commands` in order. Set `CASE` from `data.workflowRunId`
of the `workflow start` line; every later line names it. The judge and validate lines
are absent when a closed case with the same plan and base commit is continued
(`--inherit`). A frame that is about to be exceeded is a stop and a question in the
decision-question template, never a quiet widening.

## Owner-first and parked slices

A slice whose paths are data, migrations or `.fgos` state is classified
`ask-owner-first` (`critical`) and is never dispatched: the question names it and the
owner decides, slice by slice. A slice that depends on it is parked behind it. A slice
may not write the whole repository (`.`, `**`): name the directories. Writing
everything is the owner's own decision, not a proposal.

## Refusals and what to do

| Refusal | What it means and what to do |
|---|---|
| `propose-source`, `propose-slices-unreadable`, `propose-guide-missing` | Wrong call, exit 4 and stderr only: give exactly one of `--slices` or `--request`; the file must be JSON; the guide must be a conductor guide. |
| `manifest-invalid`, `slice-invalid`, `slice-verify-missing`, `slice-cycle`, `input-missing`, `plan-missing`, `option-invalid`, `request-invalid` | The list or an option does not match this table. Fix the named field and propose again. |
| `unresolved-scope`, `write-path-invalid`, `slice-write-invalid`, `write-path-forbidden`, `write-path-missing`, `write-scope-empty` | A write path cannot be judged or is not allowed (outside the repository, a symlink, `.git`, `node_modules`, run state, the whole repository, a new file whose directory is absent, a glob naming nothing). Name real files or directories. |
| `write-overlap` | Two slices write the same path, including a test added to both. Merge them or make their paths disjoint. |
| `test-scan-too-wide` | The slice changes so much code that its tests cannot be sized. Split it. |
| `capability-unregistered` | A capability is not registered in the runner config. Pick one from `../../_shared/capability-catalog.md`. |
| `rigor-below-floor`, `slice-rigor-below-table`, `slice-raise-invalid`, `slice-raise-needs-reason` | A rigor may only be raised, with a reason, to a value of `low`, `standard`, `high`, `critical`. |
| `gate-command-missing` | Declare `capabilities.code:implement.verify` in the runner config; the final gate runs only that command. |
| `guide-activity-missing` | The guide lacks an activity the commands need; use `coding/feature` or ask. |
| `code-slice-below-standard`, `pattern-unresolved`, `launch-bound-unknown`, `frame-defaults-missing`, `slice-writes-missing`, `slice-table-invalid` | The catalog, the table or the guide is inconsistent with the proposal. This is a blocker for the owner, not something to patch around. |
